g1_ledger#2.killer: Share of the offloaded KV that can be fetched over PCIe each decode step without stalling. This applies when many users run long contexts at once, which is the "3× users" regime the idea claims. I took 30% resident and FP8 KV on Llama-3.1-8B (64 KB/token)
g1_ledger#2.why: In the multi-user regime it is pitched for, the step stalls on PCIe by about 3.5×, and in the single-request regime where the bandwidth fits, it saves only about 1.2×.

g1_ledger#1.killer: Load time from the slowest tier compared with recomputing prefill, for 20K tokens on Llama-3.1-8B (2.62 GB KV in BF16, 425 TFLOP prefill)
g1_ledger#1.why: The physics has 2–16× headroom and outputs are exact, but this is already current practice (vLLM + LMCache). On real traces, the gain over GPU-only prefix caching is about 1.2×, not 2.4×.

g1_ledger#3.killer: How small an accuracy change a 30-minute RULER-128K check can detect. At about 28 GPU-s per 128K sample, that budget gives about 32 samples per configuration
g1_ledger#3.why: The 30-minute check can only catch the "major" R1-Distill case, not a "meaningful" Gemma-3 loss, and it adds no gain over the existing FP8 default.

g1_mech#3.killer: Whether the FP8 failure is confined to a few layers. Per-layer gating only pays off if the share f of layers kept in BF16 is small (f ≤ 0.5 for RATIO ≥ 1.1) and probe KL predicts the RULER loss
g1_mech#3.why: It is cheap and can be falsified with stock vLLM flags, but it only helps on the few models where FP8 fails, and then by at most about 1.2×. If the failures come from the kernel rather than from particular layers, gating reverts to all-BF16.

g1_rf1#1.killer: token hit rate h on a real trace (the idea's own kill line is h < 0.4)
g1_rf1#1.why: It is the tool a competent practitioner already runs, so it adds 1.0× over best practice, and even against no reuse it gives about 1.3× on a public trace, below its own 1.3× line.

g1_mech#1.killer: end-to-end throughput gain at h=0.5 (its own kill line is <1.5×)
g1_mech#1.why: It describes shipping LMCache/vLLM behaviour, and it fails its own 1.5× line by arithmetic: 66% prefill × 50% hits caps the gain at 1.49×.

g1_rf2#1.killer: its stated falsifier: hit TTFT over NVMe must be ≥3× lower than vLLM's GPU-only prefix cache at a matched hit rate
g1_rf2#1.why: Its falsifier is impossible by construction, and the mechanism (native FP8 bytes, tiered, layer-pipelined) is LMCache's existing disk path.

g1_rf2#3.killer: hit-weighted FLOPs gained over LRU when the working set is compared with tier capacity (its own kill line is <15%)
g1_rf2#3.why: A better eviction policy only helps when capacity is short, and SSD tiers make capacity cheap, so the system-level gain is about 2–5% even if the 15% target is met.
